questions.q: What does Fabric's Monitoring Hub actually unify?
options: Notebook runs, pipeline runs, Dataflow refreshes, and other item activity, all in one list instead of separate per-item history pages
Only notebook runs, nothing else
Only Unity Catalog access grants
Only billing information across capacities
questions.explain: This does the same job as Databricks & Delta Lake Lesson 11's Run History, but across every item type at once.

questions.q: What information does one row in the Monitoring Hub typically show?
options: Item name, type, status, start time, and duration — filterable by item type, status, or time range
Only the item's name, with no status information
Only whether Git integration is enabled for that item
Only billing cost, with no run status
questions.explain: This makes it a genuinely useful first stop for answering "did last night's pipeline actually run?"

questions.q: What does drilling into a failed run in the Monitoring Hub reveal?
options: Nothing; the Monitoring Hub cannot show run-level detail
The exact CU cost of the failed run, with no error information
The actual error message, which activity or cell failed, and which downstream activities never ran because of it
Only a generic "failed" label with no further detail
questions.explain: This is the same triage instinct — read the actual error before guessing at a cause.

questions.q: How does the Monitoring Hub relate to Databricks & Delta Lake's job Run History?
options: Only Fabric has ever needed to answer this question
They are completely unrelated concepts with no real similarity
They solve the exact same operational question — what ran, when, did it succeed — just at different scopes: per-job there, tenant-wide here
The Monitoring Hub replaces the need for any run history concept in Databricks
questions.explain: Neither platform invented the concept from scratch — both answer the same real operational need.

questions.q: Why is checking the Monitoring Hub a better first step than guessing at what went wrong?
options: The Monitoring Hub only shows successful runs, never failures
It shows the real, specific error and failure point, rather than requiring speculation about the cause
Guessing is actually the recommended first step according to this lesson
The Monitoring Hub always fixes the error automatically once viewed
questions.explain: This mirrors the same triage-first instinct that later production-practice material in this course builds on directly.
